decisions.id: accepted gap (i): the moved foreground call
decisions.summary: A live hold's foreground call that outlives its move to the background and then writes held text through shared text alone now passes the pre-call refusal, and nothing writes it back.
decisions.why: Judged on its own. The hold exists so that no verdict is recorded for plan text other than the text reviewed. That purpose is still enforced mechanically: make plan-verdict refuses a verdict whose section digest moved. So the gap's outcome is a re-run review (about 1-4 minutes), not a wrong verdict, and the hold is not gutted. For the measured case (subagents' calls) the write-back cannot follow the call: the harness gives a moved subagent call no end event (39 of 39 measured, no BgEnd), so there is nothing to restore at. That is a limit the guard cannot get around, not an inconvenience. Measured at 0 of 39 moved calls writing plan.md. The only full cover would be to keep refusing shared text for every foreground call, which restores the defect being fixed.

decisions.summary: A foreground command that detaches its writer (&, nohup, setsid, disown) and writes held text after the shell returns, quoting only shared text, now passes with no write-back.
decisions.why: Judged on its own. A detached process's write after the shell returns cannot be seen by a hook that runs at that return, so the write-back could never cover it. Before T78 it was refused only by accident, when its command happened to quote shared template text; one quoting nothing held already passed. The final outcome is still guarded by plan-verdict's digest refusal, at the cost of a re-review, not a wrong verdict. Alternative (c), refusing the narrowing when the command detaches, is a cheaper partial cover that was turned down on a design ground (a second detach reader). That ground alone would not justify an exception, but no exception is needed here: the case that remains open is not a wrong outcome. It is a bounded rework cost, caught by a real mechanical refusal.

decisions.why: This is T79's own line: the defects it names, fixed. Unchanged from the last round.

decisions.summary: A brace expansion stays in its word. $(pwd) or `pwd` is the shell's place. A loop's, if's or function's body is read past its keyword. A target's segment starts at its command (bind::from_command, shown). gate-write's head_of reads past timeout N.
decisions.why: Each is a found defect fixed in the task (fix as we go), and each puts a verdict where bash puts the write. Re-probed through bin-r4 in this reviewer's run: for-loop, if and function bodies writing the mirror are now refused (HEAD passed the first two).

decisions.summary: The arm for an unresolved place is replaced. The walk first resolves what the command's text resolves (literal loop values, an unassigned name as empty or the guard's environment, ${N:?}/${N:-W}/${N%lit}, dirname/basename of a known X, $PWD after each cd, bodies of loops, ifs and functions). What stays unknown (read/mapfile/printf -v/+=, a loop over a substitution, $RANDOM, past source/eval, a substitution's value) keeps spec 204's D6.
decisions.why: This is the cure the last round asked for. Re-run in this reviewer's run through /tmp/t79/bin-r4 standing in the mirror, sid t and nobody: all five probes are refused or rewritten. So are last round's other forms that passed: cp /tmp/a $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/f, echo x > $(echo /diagram)/f, touch $(basename /tmp/q/x), cd $(somewhere) && git commit. For what stays unknown, D6 is spec 204's conservative direction. The 29 bx rows pass, 29 of 29 for each sid (r4.b29.{t,nobody}.tsv, re-counted). The one form still passed, cp /tmp/a "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/f", is a quoted word holding a shell character, which is T83's class (ruled below). The other three passes are no write at all, as bash runs them: echo x > $UNSET/f, sed -i s/a/b/ $F and cp /tmp/a $DEST.

decisions.summary: A name nobody assigns takes its value in the guard's environment, else empty. So $UNSET/f is /f, and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is read as the project's directory although the Bash tool's shell leaves it unset.
decisions.why: This is where bash puts the write, as ruled last round. The premise is measured: the names only the Bash tool's shell sets (CLAUDE_JOB_DIR, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS, the messaging socket, GIT_EDITOR, and others) are none of them a place in the mirror. That was re-read in this reviewer's shell. The recorded env-shell.txt holds names only, and a grep of it for /diagram is empty. The CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR misreading errs in the refusing direction, and the command it refuses writes /f, which is not good work. Not a defect.

decisions.summary: cd $UNSET is read as bash's cd with no word, that is $HOME, so cd $UNSET && git commit standing in the mirror is now allowed. Spec 204 FR-002 listed an unassigned variable as unresolvable, and its acceptance line names this exact command as not allowed silently.
decisions.why: This narrows spec 204 FR-002's letter, though constraint 2 calls FR-002 kept. D6's stated purpose is that the precision fix cannot become a bypass into main, and it does not here. In this reviewer's shell, bash -c 'cd /tmp; cd $UNSET && pwd' printed /home/agent, so the commit lands in $HOME, not in the mirror. The probe through bin-r4 is allowed, and HEAD refused it. The same yardstick passed $UNSET/f -> /f. The true unknown (cd $(somewhere)) stays refused and pinned. The block's cost paragraph discloses the change.

decisions.summary: git clone $R and git worktree add --detach $W, with R and W unset, are no write. git -C /x/$U commit is not in the mirror. Their unresolved pins move to $(cat url), $(cat w) and git -C <mirror>/$U.
decisions.why: Each pin moves to what bash and git do: a usage error with no tree made, or a place outside the mirror. The unresolved forms stay pinned under D6. Ruled the same way last round.

decisions.summary: Pins move in gm_tree_hooks, main_tree_hooks, readme_hooks (with its shell twins) and gate_write_hooks, plus main-tree fixture row 59 (rewrote -> allowed). Each keeps its old meaning through a form that stays unknown (read NAME, cd $(somewhere)).
decisions.why: A verdict changing as a bug is fixed is expected (fix as we go). Each moved pin either keeps its fail-closed meaning through a truly unknown form or moves to where bash writes.

decisions.summary: A name assigned more than once is judged at each of its values. D=/diagram/x; D=/tmp/y; touch $D/f standing in the mirror, a scratch write that HEAD passed, is now refused. The block lists this under 'its measured cost in full', not under Found and left.
decisions.why: It closes a real false allow (F=/diagram/a; echo x > $F; F=/tmp/b) and judges if/else branches both ways, which is good. But the refusal it leaves is a wrong outcome, a check refusing good work (constitution XIV v2.36.0). It contradicts the block's own goal 1, 'no scratch write refused because a variable stands in its name'. It is newly introduced: HEAD allowed it and bin-r4 refuses it (p1.r4.tsv row 22, re-run). It is not impossible to avoid, because the command's text shows a straight-line reassignment with no branch between. Last round held that 'none in the corpus' counts how often a wrong verdict happens, not whether it is wrong, and the same standard applies here. The refusing direction makes it cheaper, but not exempt from FR-009. The cure needs no code: carry it as a Found and left item with why it is not fixed here, a filed task id and its order (FR-009). Fixing it in T79 is the other cure.

decisions.summary: The walk binds a many-valued name up to 64 values. Past that, it falls back. The block does not say to what, and the cost paragraph does not list it.
decisions.why: Measured in this reviewer's run through bin-r4 and bin-head, standing in the mirror, sid nobody, main-tree alone and all guards. A loop over 65 or 70 literal scratch values (for f in /tmp/q/1 ... /tmp/q/70; do touch $f; done) is refused by bin-r4 and allowed by HEAD. 63 values pass. So past the cap the name falls to D6. That keeps the mirror safe (a mirror value in position 1 or 70 is refused, as is a nested '.' value), but it refuses scratch work HEAD passed. The block calls its cost paragraph 'its measured cost in full', and it does not list this. The 'what stays unknown' list does not name the cap either. Bounding the work is a fair design, but the wrong outcome it leaves must be stated and either fixed (judge a single name's values linearly, for example) or carried as a Found and left item with why, a filed id and its order (FR-009). The block must also name the cap's fallback.

decisions.summary: A quoted word holding a space or a shell character is blanked, so the destination is misread. cp /tmp/a "/diagram/x y" passes, and so does cp /tmp/a "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/f" (re-probed). Left as T83, to land before T22.
decisions.why: This is a pre-existing defect. The why is concrete: the blanking keeps commit messages, sed scripts and programs from being read as paths by every guard, so a fix needs its own corpus replay. It is filed with an id and an order (FR-009).

decisions.summary: make-only refuses a guard file's name (Makefile, dev/work-budget.json, a guard's source) written into a $(mktemp -d) place or a scratch copy in a loop's body (12 replay moves). Left as T87, to land before T22.
decisions.why: HEAD refuses the same write to a literal scratch path. The rule is the guard-file list's, read by layer 3 and make-only alike, outside the walk. It carries why, a filed id and an order.

decisions.summary: A python3 -c program that writes a place it computes from sys.argv is judged where the shell stands. Now that loop bodies are seen, three corpus scratch writes are newly refused (bx#54240, bx#58694, ux#2209). Left as T89, to land before T22.
decisions.why: HEAD refuses the same program outside a loop. These three refusals come from fixing a false allow (unseen loop bodies), and keeping that false allow would be the worse defect. The rule is py_c's, outside the walk, and needs its own replay. It carries why, a filed id and an order.

decisions.summary: gate-write reads a target's command from a segment cut at 120 characters. A make behind long VAR=value prefixes, in a loop's body, is newly refused (ux#1371). Left as T90, to land before T22.
decisions.why: HEAD refuses the same line outside a loop. The why is concrete: readme_hooks' kept-segment rule reads the cut, so the fix is a field of its own on the target. It carries why, a filed id and an order.

decisions.summary: readme_hooks.rs substitutes $(mktemp) itself, as the walk now does. Not filed.
decisions.why: The two agree, so there is no wrong outcome. A difference that works is not a defect.

decisions.summary: house-style's /tmp/ 'outside' prefix makes three replay moves an artifact of a mirror under /tmp. On their real paths, a direct run shows both binaries correcting them.
decisions.why: A limit of the measurement, named so the moves are read correctly. Not a defect of the guard.

decisions.id: T80 fix: section_places / held_places / write_back by place
decisions.summary: A task's section is read as the places its own headings stand (ordered_sections rebuilt on them, output unchanged and pinned); the snapshot keeps one text per place and write_back restores each changed place by byte span, paired by order when counts match, else by heading, never writing an old text holding a place's heading past its first line.
decisions.why: This is the task's own line (restore each held place through plan_text's section reading). The pairing rule is design inside that ask, not a narrowing of it.

decisions.summary: The answer stays the same for a one-place section and for a block hold; for a split section it names the places written back, names any place not found or new after NOT written back, and says NOTHING of it is written back when nothing was restored.
decisions.why: The task line asks that the answer say what was restored. A different message for the split case is what was asked, and leaving the one-place message unchanged narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The refusal keeps judging a write against the joined section (T78's pin). Only the write-back changes. The refusal's own defect, where a split section is judged by joined text so an unchanged Write is refused, is filed as T120, ordered to land before T22.
decisions.why: A known defect is left: under a split section's hold, the refusal rejects an unchanged Write, which is a check refusing good work, measured in /tmp/t80/write-T22.out. That makes this a narrowing and not just a difference. Two of the section's reasons cannot carry the ruling on their own. 'T80's line is the write-back' is the session's own scope, and 'flips a pin T78 set today' preserves existing behavior. What carries it: the GM approved briefs that DEFAULT to fixing in the task (request item 4), and a default implies a reasoned exception. The accepted spec gives that exception its form in FR-009 (why, the filed id, the order), and the section meets all three: why stated, T120, 'lands before T22'. Purpose test: the purpose is fewer re-rounds and no defects silently carried. T80 closes the harmful half, a false 'written back' that left text corrupted or doubled. The deferred half fails safe, since it refuses where it should pass and the refusal can be escaped. It reaches none of 451's own sections (0 of the 8 split sections are in 451's plan, measured 2026-11-21, /tmp/t80/split.py). It also changes a pin reviewed today, so it needs its own red-first change and review and should not ride in a write-back fix. It is filed and ordered, not dropped. Caveat: from this bundle I cannot tell which T22 'lands before T22' means. The only T22 the block names is 444's, the measured hold subject, and I cannot see whether that task is open. The ruling assumes the order means 451's T22 and names a real, still-open task. If it does not, the deferral has no order and this ruling does not hold.

Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.why: Enforcement of what the test exists to catch (the step limit regression, mutant M1); it adds no behavior and only fails when the thing it guards is absent.

decisions.summary: Scope: the test file alone - no engine code, no guard code, T88's and T93's files untouched.
decisions.why: Confines the fix to the defect; narrows nothing the request or spec asked for.

decisions.summary: Found and left: eight other test files carrying the same 20 s wall bound, not filed, because none has failed by it outside T185's own red-first run (measured census).

decisions.summary: an id a list item or heading already gives keeps that text; a dashless restatement of it is commentary and is not read over it
decisions.why: This keeps every existing correct read unchanged (the brief's constraint) and does not cut anything T82 asked for. The dashless ids T82 targets (287 in 21 specs) have no other form.

That makes this a narrowing and not just a difference. Two of the section's reasons cannot carry the ruling on their own. What carries it: the GM approved briefs that DEFAULT to fixing in the task (request item 4), and a default implies a reasoned exception. It reaches none of 451's own sections (0 of the 8 split sections are in 451's plan, measured 2026-11-21, /tmp/t80/split.py). It also changes a pin reviewed today, so it needs its own red-first change and review and should not ride in a write-back fix. It is filed and ordered, not dropped. The ruling assumes the order means 451's T22 and names a real, still-open task. If it does not, the deferral has no order and this ruling does not hold.

decisions.summary: The million-step spelling test's 20 s wall-clock recv_timeout is replaced by a bound on the search thread's own CPU time (schedstat's first field, polled every 100 ms), failing past CPU_BOUND_NS; a panicked search thread fails at once.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md or 451's FR-001 to FR-013 settles this test's bound, so the choice of measure is the task's own. The block reports T81's line as asking that the bound count steps not wall time, or a ceiling sized for a loaded host; fancy_regex 0.14 exposes no step count but the limit firing (the block's reading of its vm.rs), so the thread's CPU time is the work measure. It keeps the bound's filed purpose (T185's section: a spin fails rather than hangs) - M2 still fails, at 30022000592 ns of CPU - and ends the refusal of good work the block measured (6 reds by name, 33 of 88 under load.sh 88). A check that refuses good work is a defect under XIV, and fixing it is the task.

decisions.summary: CPU_BOUND_NS is 30 s, a CONVENTION and a knob, with its why beside it (10x the scan's 3.2 s on the slowest core, 4x its 7.4 s worst at 88 copies).
decisions.why: Choosing the ceiling's value is the task's own design choice, labeled as a convention with its measured basis; no research claim moves and the spec settles no value.

decisions.summary: The test also builds the house style's pattern shape with fancy_regex's old 1,000,000-step limit and asserts it errs on the text, so the text stays past the limit the test exists for.
decisions.why: Enforcement only: it makes the test keep testing what it was filed to test (the step limit), the 'pin the step budget by counting steps' half of T81's line; deleting the test's purpose would leave it nothing to check.

decisions.summary: No engine code and no guard code change: the house_style_hooks test file alone; T88's set_down_hooks, T88's land crate and T93's event_log_hooks/fields.rs untouched.
decisions.why: The defect is in the test's bound, not the scan: the block's slowed run cut HEAD's scan off at 1.25 s of CPU, and the 55 green loaded runs used 3.5-6.1 s each, both far under any spin. The brief bounds the files. Nothing the request or FR-013 asks is cut by it.

decisions.summary: Eight other test files carrying the same 20 s wall bound (four in rust/guard/shared, three in the guard, one in reviews) are neither changed nor filed.
decisions.why: Under constitution XIV as the GM ruled 2026-11-19, a defect is a wrong outcome. The block censused the class (others.py, plus a --- FAILED census of every transcript) and found no transcripted failure of any of the eight but T185's own red-first run of 2026-11-19T02:05Z. Its unattributed reds (two guard-crate Phase reds at 20 s or more, named by no transcript, and the 13:56Z row) name no test, as the block itself says a long run alone does not. So no wrong outcome of these eight is measured. This crate's four take 0.2-0.66 s alone against this test's 1.6 s, and the other four were not timed. A latent difference with no measured wrong outcome is not a known defect, so fix-as-we-go does not reach it and leaving it is not a narrowing. The block names the CPU bound as the form to copy if one goes red.

A check that goes red on good work under load costs builders re-runs: the block counts 6 such reds by name, at a load reading of 82.78 taken between them. The GM asked that performance work come first (2026-11-20).
